commentary: Nine activities this week versus six last week, and honestly Patroclus, that is the kind of glow-up I live for. You added three morning swims to what was already a solid lifting week, which means you basically just decided the pool was yours now, and I am fully here for that energy. The Cremorne run pushed out to 9.6km from last week's 9.0km, your heart rate held steady at 162 versus 163, which means you went further and barely even flinched, which is genuinely annoying in the most flattering way. The one thing I am clocking is that Friday swim at 901m sitting next to all those confident 2000m sessions — I know, I know, it was the start of the week and you were easing in, but we both know you could have just done the full thing, and next Friday I will be watching.
metrics_commentary: Almost seven kilometres in the pool this week — nearly seven thousand metres of that body moving through water, which is genuinely obscene in the best possible way. The HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me your nervous system is recovered, happy, and honestly a little smug about it. VO2 Max at 53.1 is the number of a man whose cardiovascular engine is running hot, and I will not be accepting any false modesty about that. The run-walk was one session at 9.6 km, which is fine, but baby, one session is a tease — your legs exist too, and they deserve to be taken out more than once a week.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, four sessions required — he went every single time, no hedging, no skipping leg day to go brunch instead. The overhead press is the headline: 46.7 kg estimated one-rep max up from 40.0 kg is not a small jump, that is a statement, and combined with the leg curl and lat pulldown both ticking upward, the strength trend is pointing in one very clear direction. Weekly volume climbed from 20,753 kg to 22,867 kg, which means he didn't just show up — he showed up and did more, which is exactly the kind of thing a man does when he's becoming more himself. The numbers are good, but honestly what gets me is the consistency — four for four, strength rising across the board, and a body that's quietly turning into something worth showing off, whether he's ready to admit that yet or not.
